clue.text: Saintly lady who affected one vicar badly

indicators.note: done badly, the letters of one and vicar are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A holy woman whose presence shook a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Veronica is the woman said to have wiped Christ's face on the way to Calvary.

clue.text: Stick it out! Finish the course on the river

parts.note: to finish is to end
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Encouragement to a rower: keep going to the end of the river course.
explanation.walkthrough: The URE is a river in North Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick it out is to persevere, bearing hardship to the end.

clue.text: Troubled tour to the Orient was most extravagant

indicators.note: troubled suggests the letters of tour being stirred up into another order

parts.note: the Orient is the East, abbreviated E

explanation.surface: A disrupted tour of Asia proved very lavish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Troubled' signals the anagram; 'was most' is padding before an adjective definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré means beyond the bounds of convention, eccentric or over the top.

clue.text: Irate about dirt-very annoyed!

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of irate and dirt are mixed

explanation.surface: Someone furious about dirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Being irritated is being vexed and cross.

clue.text: Two chaps got a lot of cattle fodder

parts.note: Alf is a short man's name, Alfred
the second chap is another Alf

explanation.surface: A couple of men bought a lot of animal feed.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucerne, a clover-like plant, is grown widely as feed for livestock.

clue.text: One member in the sick bay of the boat

indicators.note: in signals that one piece sits inside the sick bay

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a sick bay
one is the article a
MP is Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A crew member lies in the boat's infirmary.
explanation.definitionFit: A sampan is a small flat-bottomed Chinese vessel.

clue.text: Marksmen feel uncomfortable in a boat

indicators.note: in places the feeling inside the vessel

parts.note: SS is a steamship
to be hot is to feel uncomfortable from heat

explanation.surface: Snipers getting seasick on a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A good shot is a skilled rifleman, so the plural names sharpshooters.

clue.text: Someone sent Reg back after the first of May at a German city

indicators.note: the first of picks the opening letter of May

parts.note: Essen is a city in the Ruhr

indicators.note: back means the name Reg is read in reverse

explanation.surface: Someone dispatched Reg back to meet in a German city in early May.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' signals the reversal of the name; ESSEN is a city in Germany's Ruhr.
explanation.definitionFit: A courier is a person dispatched to carry word.

clue.text: Even marginal differences can be startling

indicators.note: differences suggests the letters of marginal made different, rearranged

explanation.surface: Even small variations may be disturbing.
explanation.walkthrough: MARGINAL, rearranged, gives the answer; 'Even' just helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Something alarming causes fright or sudden worry.

clue.text: On paper, he's the head…

parts.note: on a newspaper the person in charge of content is its chief, not a head on a body

explanation.surface: Someone who is the boss only in theory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On paper' looks like 'in theory' but means at a newspaper; the ellipsis runs into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief journalist at a newspaper directs and approves its content.

clue.text: and this paper is on the head of an idiot

parts.note: fool's means belonging to an idiot
a cap is worn on the head

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: this sheet sits on a dunce's head.
explanation.walkthrough: A paper size is named after the jester's cap once used as its watermark.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolscap is a large size of writing sheet, around 13 by 16 inches.

clue.text: Dishevelled relation arrives from China

indicators.note: dishevelled means messed up, so the letters of relation are tousled into a new order

explanation.surface: An untidy relative turns up from the Far East.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental means of the East, as Chinese things are.

clue.text: Gases given off by ship about eleven perhaps

indicators.note: about means the ship surrounds the side

parts.note: SS is a steamship
an eleven, as in football or cricket, is a team

explanation.surface: A ship releasing exhaust around eleven o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eleven' looks like a time but is a side of eleven players.
explanation.definitionFit: Vapour rising from boiling water is the sense here, in the plural.

clue.text: Net straining horribly, but it refuses to budge

indicators.note: horribly means the letters of net straining are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A net stretched to bursting point, yet it will not move.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone intransigent is stubborn and unwilling to give way.

clue.text: I'm a clever chap with a weapon although it might not be adjusted correctly

definitions.text: although it might not be adjusted correctly

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
a lance is a long spear

explanation.surface: A boastful graduate with a spear, though perhaps not well balanced.
explanation.definitionFit: An imbalance is a lack of proportion that wants correcting.

clue.text: The French region about which to make a choice

indicators.note: about means the region goes round the French article

parts.note: a section is a part or region
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Choosing which French district to pick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container; 'which to make' joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A selection is something picked out from several options.

clue.text: Find beds for the elderly around the start of Winter in an upland area

indicators.note: around means the beds and elderly go round the opening letter

parts.note: cots are small beds
the old are the elderly

indicators.note: the start of picks the first letter of Winter

explanation.surface: Locate care-home beds near the start of winter in hill country.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cotswolds are a range of hills in south-west central England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cotswolds are rolling limestone hills in England.

clue.text: Does he blind the constable with his eye catching style?

parts.note: a bobby is British slang for a policeman
one who blinds with light is a dazzler

explanation.surface: Asking whether a flashy dresser blinds the police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: A BOBBY is a British police constable; a bobby-dazzler is northern English slang for a striking, splendid person.
explanation.definitionFit: A bobby-dazzler is someone remarkable or showily impressive.

clue.text: Zola set about the enthusiasts

indicators.note: about means the letters of Zola set are moved around

explanation.surface: The novelist Zola surrounded by keen supporters.
explanation.definitionFit: Zealots are fanatical followers of a cause.

clue.text: Use Eastern slate to make gravestones

indicators.note: to make signals the letters being formed into something new

explanation.surface: Using slate from the East for headstones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' rearranges SLATE into STELA; E for Eastern ends the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Stelae are upright carved stone slabs, often grave markers.

clue.text: Shelter provided for protection

definitions.meaning: a refuge or place of safety
safety granted, as political protection to a refugee

explanation.definitionFit: Asylum is both a sanctuary and the refuge granted by a state.

clue.text: Measure time

definitions.meaning: the rhythm or beat of verse or music

explanation.definitionFit: A metre is a unit of length and also the beat pattern of poetry.

clue.text: Bill's stories!

definitions.meaning: bills are invoices, so the plural sense

explanation.definitionFit: Accounts are invoices to pay and also narrated versions of events.

clue.text: Thinkers can't begin to be employers!

indicators.note: cannot begin means the first letter of the thinkers' word is dropped

parts.note: musers are people who ponder

explanation.surface: Philosophers unable to get started as bosses.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is one who employs something, puts it to use.

clue.text: Instrument to hold ice cream perhaps

parts.note: a cornet is a brass instrument

explanation.surface: A musical instrument holding an ice cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cornet' is also a British ice cream cone, a neat surface twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornetto is a well-known brand of cone-shaped frozen dessert.

clue.text: Ladies who make perfect models

indicators.note: who make signals the letters being reshaped into something else

explanation.surface: Women who are flawless fashion models.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideals are standards of perfection to aim for.

clue.text: Stick a poster in this place

parts.note: a poster is an advertisement, ad
here means in this place

explanation.surface: Instruction to put a bill up on this spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to cling fast.

clue.text: There's something not right in taking a nun about

indicators.note: about means the nun goes round the word in

parts.note: a nun is addressed as Sister

explanation.surface: Something suspicious about bringing a nun along.
explanation.walkthrough: Sinister is Latin for left, as in heraldry, so 'not right' is fair as well as meaning ominous.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister in heraldry means on the left side, the opposite of dexter.
